Components

Three reading altitudes

"How it works" on the index page is written at three depths. Each is a component with construction rules, checked by python3 tools/altitude_lint.py (standard library only). Exec is the default.

python3 tools/altitude_lint.py

Exec

Construction rules

  • At most two sentences.
  • The outcome and the risk it removes. No mechanism.
  • No code, file names or line numbers.
  • The default view.

Specimen, from index.html

Staff get a fast, sourced answer to any RFP question, with the clause quoted beside it. The risk it removes is a wrong number or a stale, pre-amendment value reaching a proposal: anything it can't prove from the text, it doesn't say.

Operational

Construction rules

  • Exactly three steps.
  • Each step opens with a bold lead.
  • How it works in plain terms; no file:line references.

Specimen, from index.html

  1. Parse with rules, not a model. Clauses are numbered; an amendment that revises 7.1 is recorded as superseding it.
  2. Find clauses by keyword search with stemming and a small glossary.
  3. Ask a model to pick clauses and write one sentence, then check it in code before anyone sees it.

Surgical

Construction rules

  • The real pipeline, in order.
  • Every step names a code element and a file:line.
  • Each cited line must exist in the source, so the page fails the lint if the code moves.
  • Says where each gate fires and what the fast path skips.

Specimen, from index.html

At load, loader.load (source/loader.py:27) reads each file through parse.parse (source/rfp/parse.py:64) into store.ingest (source/rfp/store.py:62); resolve.classify (source/rfp/resolve.py:45) records what each amendment clause revises, and store.governing (store.py:112) later returns the text in force. Each question then runs answer() (source/rfp/answer.py:213), called by answer_question (mcp/server.py:50):

  1. Length cap (answer.py:214): over 2,000 characters is an error, no model call.
  2. Scope (answer.py:217): the DRAFT and VERDICT patterns (answer.py:197, 201) refuse drafting and bid calls before any model call.
  3. Fast path (answer.py:221, fast_path at :162): a plain key-fact question is answered from the governing text itself. It skips retrieval, the model and the verbatim check, since the answer is the clause. It is never taken when an unclassified amendment touches the clause (:168).
  4. Retrieve (answer.py:224): retrieve (:93) ranks clauses, and expand_with_amendments (:111) adds every amendment that replaced one.
  5. Payload cap (answer.py:234): too much text means no model call.
  6. Model call (answer.py:239): any provider failure returns unavailable with the relevant clauses and no answer (:245); unreadable output is an error (:252).
  7. Citations (answer.py:307): if none of the model's clause ids exist, nothing is answered. Cited base clauses pull in their amendments again.
  8. Drafted anyway (answer.py:323): DRAFTED (:204) withholds model text that drafts or decides.
  9. Verbatim figures (answer.py:330 to 337): every $, date and % must appear in a cited clause, and a superseded value without its replacement fails; the summary is then withheld.
